messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 ALERT  Multiple inference containers restarting in us-west-2. Symptoms: CUDA OOM during prefill path, followed by container restarts and a node flap. Affected endpoint: /v1/chat.generate. Paging: Jordan K. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefill-oom

Jordan K: taking page. joining bridge in 90s. tagging eng-runtime and ops_sre.

Mei Z: seeing repeated OOM on pod gen-3a2f (node gpu-node-21). Log excerpt:
```
2026-03-10T22:46:39Z runtime ERROR: cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at /runtime/kv_cache.cu:412
Model: rwd-alpha-1.2, request_id=req-f3b9
Attempted to reserve 38.6 GiB for kv cache expansion. GPU total: 48 GiB, free: 4.1 GiB.
Trace: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
  at prefill_expand (/srv/runtime/prefill.c:408)
```
Pod restarted ~7x in 12m. After first restart, another node (gpu-node-19) showed high GPU utilisation then flapped (kubelet OOM eviction).

eng-runtime: triage note: prefill path tries to allocate proportional to seq_len * kv_element_bytes. We saw a combination of long-context user prompts (40k-60k tokens) and certain model map configs that set kv_element_bytes to 512B due to tensor layout mismatch in v1.2. This caused >30GB allocation attempt. No graceful rejection path existed.

Jordan K: immediate plan: 1) apply gateway admission policy to reject or cap prefill tokens > 16k for public endpoints 2) toggle model-level feature flag to turn off kv caching for rwd-alpha-1.2 3) reroute obviously long requests to a worker pool that runs on q8 quantized instances. Executing now.

ops_sre: applying envoy admission patch (canary 15%): /infra/envoy/prefill_blocker_canary.yaml. Command: `kubectl apply -f /infra/envoy/prefill_blocker_canary.yaml -n prod`. Proxy will return 413 with guidance header when x-prefill-length > 16000.

deploy-bot: canary deployed: prefill_max=16000 for route /v1/chat.generate. feature_flag.kv_cache[rwd-alpha-1.2]=off at 15% traffic.

Mei Z: after canary, new pods created under updated config show no OOM. Existing pods still crashloop because their KV allocations are already resident on GPU.

eng-runtime: hotfix queued: add immediate mem-pressure handler that on SIGUSR1 triggers KV cache trimming (lru-based) rather than full process exit. Will push to canary after this incident. Also adding early rejection (413) before allocation attempt.

ops_sre: draining gpu-node-21 to recover and reprovision: `kubectl drain gpu-node-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30`

CS_ops: customer impact - noticed elevated 5xxs for customers with large-context analytics jobs. Reached out to top impacted accounts (DataFold, MediQs, AcmePay). We posted a status update to affected customers: "We're mitigating GPU memory errors impacting long-context requests. We've applied temporary routing and request size limits. We'll follow up with timeline postmortem."

Jordan K: increasing canary to 50% for prefill cap and kv_cache toggle after monitoring 5m.

Rohan P: I saw a node-level flap when kubelet OOM-killed a system pod because GPU pods held most alloc. I've spun up replacement nodes in the ASG and bumped node-alloc reservations. Command: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-asg-usw2 --desired-capacity 12`

deploy-bot: promoted gateway prefill cap and feature flag to 100%. Smoke checks running.

Mei Z: restart rate dropped sharply after promoting fixes. No new OOMs observed on newly provisioned pods. Existing crashlooping pods will be evicted and recreated clean.

eng-runtime: root cause short: the runtime allowed KV cache reservation sized by client-declared sequence length without an upper bound or graceful failure mode; combined with a variant's large kv_element_bytes (layout mismatch), this caused attempts to reserve >30GB leading to immediate OOM and container restart. Secondary cause: no eviction/trimming path in runtime, so memory pressure cascaded to node-level instability.

Jordan K: handoff to Rohan P for watcher duties for next 2h. Follow-ups: 1) runtime PR to add hard prefill cap and 413 with guidance 2) implement KV LRU trimming on SIGUSR1 and async background eviction 3) add gateway unit tests and canary tests for 40k token synthetic prompts 4) infra: node reservation tweak and better OSS alert on node-level GPU pressure.

Rohan P: taking handoff. I'll watch metrics and ensure tickets are created and assigned. Adding timeline and logs to incident page.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. Duration: ~43m. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1768729999

ops_sre: created tickets: TICKET-1367 (runtime-eviction-signal), TICKET-1368 (gateway-prefill-hardcap), TICKET-1369 (node-alloc-reserve). Assigning eng-runtime and infra.

deploy-bot: health-check: inference deployment stable for 25m, restart rate normalized to baseline. :white_check_mark:

Rohan P: will file the postmortem draft and coordinate a 1-week follow-up to validate runtime patch via canary. Closing on-call handoff now. 

Jordan K: nice work team, thanks for the fast turnaround. Pinning logs and the zoom link in this thread. :tada:
